Guru: Listen to what I am going to say. Then the doubt will be cleared.
Question: I have worked in many ashrams and institutions. What I see here is a method different from those. That itself is my doubt.
Guru: That is not your doubt. It is indeed the truth.
Question: That is what I need to know.

Guru: That knowledge cannot be obtained just by being told; it must be known through belief over a period of time. The Trimurti system and the Shaiva, Shaktheya, and Vaishnava methods of worship seen today have not only misled the people but also impoverished and alienated Bharath (India) itself. Even today, we accept the rule of others and call it our own.
Question: Why did you say it belongs to others?

Guru: The English language is not ours. The attire is not ours. In short, everything is an imitation. We have lost everything of our own. Exhausted as we are, we have not yet been able to see this as the truth. As a result of arguments between early priests and kings, the Puranas were rewritten by a few immigrant scholars known as Brahmins, altering the knowledge that was in the hands of the kings. When further arguments arose through that, the Upanishads were created. They contain little reality. A few poems written by scholars and the realities written by the wise are mixed together in them. Initially, there were only the Dasha Upanishads (ten Upanishads). That became eighteen, then one hundred and eight. Now they are countless. The same goes for the Gita. Initially, there were only three hundred shlokas (verses). The rest were added over time according to the circumstances.
Question: How did you get this evidence?
Guru: Haven't you understood that this evidence is a vision (darshan)?
Question: You yourself say that visions can contain falsehoods.
Guru: I told you, I got this when I tried to correct that.
Question: How do you handle this knowledge?
Guru: There is a command to carry this knowledge forward like a Guru-disciple relationship. That is the path being followed now.
Question: Another doubt. It is about this Akhandanama (continuous chanting) which is chanted using your own name.

Guru: It is not an Akhandanama. It is a mantra. If needed, it can also be a stotra (hymn). In that sense, it can be called an Akhandanama. While receiving visions, two disciples received these lines as an ethereal voice (ashariri). 'You must strengthen this by chanting it. You will need it someday'—they came and told me that they received it this way. I did not let them do it then. The reason being, my name was in it. But those who received it used to chant it without my knowledge. The reason for that was they had received an ethereal voice saying, 'If you do not strengthen this by chanting, danger will befall you.'
Question: There is no way they could chant it without Swami knowing, right?
Guru: They would chant it loudly when I was not around. When I was present, they would do it mentally. Because of that, I was spared.
Question: Could you explain a bit about that?

Guru: It should not be explained. I can say a few things. I mentioned earlier that our attire and language are not ours. We had to adopt them because there was a lack of knowledge and action in our country. A person without knowledge cannot expand any action, can they?
Disciple: How can you say there is no knowledge—isn't our land the one with all the knowledge?
Guru: Then why did we take what belongs to others?
Question: In the past, we had universities like Nalanda and Takshashila, didn't we?

Guru: I too am saying that they existed. That language disappeared from among us because our merit (punya) diminished. When our merit diminished, we had to become slaves to the infiltration of others. They had knowledge and capability. A language like Hindi or Pali existed here. I do not know if it came about as a mixture of everything. As a renewal of that, Sanskrit was introduced. Through Sanskrit, the Puranas, Upanishads, and Vedas were written. In them, they wrote 'Amaranirjjaradeva' and turned the Brahmin into a god. Consequently, the vast majority of people came to be known as Asuras. Through some of them, the Shaktheya system was developed. Through some others, Shaivism was developed. And through yet others, Vaishnavism was developed. None of this is bad. Each is better than the other. How will you find out which of these is right and which is wrong?
Question: It cannot be found out.

Guru: That is the exact experience I had. It led me astray to a great extent. For us who are living, learning about the past is fine, but it is not something to be practiced in this era. Knowing that, what is needed is the sense of dharma to unite and work for the present time. Assimilating the bygone Vedic dharmas and karmas, mixing them in the Puranas, giving undue importance to gods and goddesses, and thereby diluting human potential—this is the result of poets and artists working together. This led to a surrender to miracles, the occult powers derived from miracles, and all kinds of activities taking refuge in them. I am a person who has experienced and known such surrenders. Bearing witness to the direct inferences I had and have experienced through that, I tell you—I am trying to present myself before you to instill courage in you, the courageous souls who have attained a truly worthy birth. May you be convinced.

Perceptual inferences (*Pratyakshanumanangal*) refer to our ancestral beliefs and their guiding principles. Direct perception (*Pratyaksham*) is a part of this. The disembodied voice, the stream of light—the only witness to recognizing them is the grace-filled, luminous streak of compassion. What and how to testify to it is solidified over time by the experiential record of that moment. There is a reason for saying 'over time'. Otherwise, a Guru is needed to explain it in that very moment. If lacking complete qualification, not only will the Guru be unable to do so, but the disciple will also fall into disarray. Because of this, many people wander astray and reach danger zones. There is evidence that they have suffered thus. Our nation was full of goodness and had reached great heights in all respects. All forms of nature here are favorable for the way of life. Nature and its elements intertwine, and humans experience its complete bliss. Other countries have not received such favorable nature. They have climates that are partially favorable, partially unfavorable, and even uninhabitable. Mahabali, the Asura emperor, is proof that our land was completely filled with goodness, blending devotion and humility, and possessed a governance system that imparted a good method of protecting the weak. The hypocritical policy that branded one who does not consume *Sura* (liquor) as an Asura insulted noble kings, transformed the one who consumes Sura into a Deva, overturned knowledge through Homa (fire rituals) and Tantric practices, diverted Dharma from virtue towards Adharma, manifested this course of action here, redirected all charities to Brahmins, thereby fostering Adharma and causing the loss of the people's merit. In the Kali Yuga, this Dharma is an absolutely harsh Adharma. The Vedic system, which did not even hesitate to write down '*Pratyakshavaham Dharmam*' by portraying all the virtuous souls as Asuras and Asura lineages while realizing the one who poured Sura as a Deva, fabricated the Puranas and Vedas and became the authority of the Upanishads. Consequently, the Asuras degraded into a state without literacy, not even feeling that the land and country belonged to them. Then, divine worship became trances, lamps, ululations, and joyous shouts at the edge of the forest, along with the consecration of ancestors under the shade of trees. Over the years, this tutelary deity system evolved into global worship. It includes Yantramoorthi, Tantramoorthi, Yogeeshwaran, Marutha, Kali, Kooli, and even the Brahmarakshas who protects Brahman. If needed, it becomes Dakshinamoorthi. Once it becomes Dakshinamoorthi, it is a wait to consecrate Uttaramoorthi. The boons received by Bhasmasura are a deception created by writing such stories. Just like the verse in the Gita, '*Pratyakshavaham Dharmam*', I too could see everything directly. Not only did it become direct, but I also received the word, and through it, illnesses were cured. Not in a trivial way—a patient treated in Singapore for eight years was cured in forty-one days. A patient in a family where the father, daughter, and daughter-in-law were doctors was cured. Their names are not disclosed as they might feel slighted. Only holy ash (Bhasma) and holy water (Theertha) were given. Even bladder cancer of that nature has been cured. Similarly, there are many direct experiences considered as spiritual realization. It was then that terrifying forms of tutelary deities and gods appeared ceremoniously with salutations in an instant, informing through those with visions that performing certain methods would yield quicker results, and we acted accordingly. After a month of this, the influx of people increased exponentially. During that time, all this began to fall apart. Not only that, all the people who had loved until then resorted to abuse, fighting, and quarrels. It was only after about seven and a half years that a correction was received for this.

During this period, an opportunity arose to uplift the place currently known as Guruvihar in Melkadakkavoor. Its rightful heirs—Sharada, Bhargavi, Lalitha, Bhargavi's husband Gopalan Master, and son Ramadas—all arrived at Varkala Santhigiri to resolve their family curse. They inquired about this. The descriptions were explained to them. Among them, madness and incurable diseases were persisting. When asked among that group, "A curse of Narayana Guru is seen. How did that happen?", they told the truth.

"There were two mothers in our group. One of them had hurt Narayana Guru. One was favorable to the Swami. We four are the children belonging to one of those branches. We had an unmarried uncle. He and the Swami were close friends. In those days, the Swami was known as Nanu Ashan. The Swami used to come and go at Kuzhivila. An artificial cave was created there. It had enough space to accommodate a table, a chair, and a sofa. One day, when the Swami arrived, the sofa and chair on which the Swami used to lie had been chopped up and thrown into the nearby deep water. This was done by the mother and her accomplices who disliked the Swami. The mirror was thrown on the floor and shattered. The heartbroken uncle said to the Swami, 'It is no longer suitable for us to sit here, let's go.' Then, he took the Swami to the house of their relative, Mundayil Kunjikrishnan Chattampi in Varkala. Walking from there through the Thoduve bridge along the canal, he sat under a jackfruit tree and worked towards what is today's Sivagiri." All this was narrated by the late Gopalan Master. He was an Anchal Master; the father of Ramadas, who is currently the Junior Health Inspector at Anchuthengu. Only a small remnant of that dilapidated artificial cave had survived. He sorrowfully told me that women now use the spot to sit out of the sun and beat coconut husks, and children use it for defecation and urination.

Then, what I felt like saying was this: "It doesn't matter, lean some long palm fronds against it, tie palm leaves to it, clean the place, and light a lamp there for six months. Then you will have some experience. After that, we can do what is necessary." Accordingly, they cleaned it and did what was required. Before the completion of six months, it was time for the Sivagiri pilgrimage. At 4:00 AM, while the milkman living there was milking the cow, light reflected on the vessel, and when he turned to look, a ball-like light was rising from the cave, from the spot where the lamp was lit. When it rose and ascended upward, dogs, cats, and cows in nearby houses created a commotion, and cows broke their ropes; this incident was experienced within a four-mile radius. This can be understood by asking the locals there.

After this, as per my suggestion that it could be renovated, they repaired it, resumed the rituals, and began to see results, at which point the old adversaries reared their heads again. When I went there, a quarrel took place. While Gopalan Master and I were hastily boarding the train from Kadakkavoor railway station, a member of this family came, struck me, snatched away my towel, and left.

Today, they are averse to recounting this history of Guru Vihar because I am its primary agent. Even now, madness and other incurable diseases continue to haunt that family, and these afflictions have not been completely eradicated. This serves as evidential proof that if spiritually blind souls lacking ancestral purity remain within a family merely to conceal the truth, that family can never be truly reformed. Consequently, those who sincerely desire reformation will be unable to attain it through their own efforts, and others will be ready to misinterpret the situation. The opponents concealed the truth, relayed false information to Chirayinkeezhu Ramakrishnan, and consequently had him write about Guru Vihar in a distorted manner. As I have stated earlier, it took me seven and a half years to discover the underlying cause of this opposition, and it took another seven years to rectify it. What I am addressing today through my own experience is the profound realization gained from that rectification. I have consequently discerned how this Trinity system originated, what anomalies exist within it, what befell the lineage of Manu, and why the memory of Manu has vanished from the hearts of the people. I shall not expound upon these matters at present.
Question: It is said that Manu is the son of Brahma, is it not?

Guru: That is exactly what I said has been corrected. It will take a considerable amount of time for you to be convinced of it. After you read some literature and become somewhat convinced, I shall explain it to you. It is a spiritual revelation, after all! Did you not observe that the very people who were granted the experience eventually harbored enmity toward me? To understand this to some extent, read the section titled '*Daivachinthanam*' authored by Narayana Guru. Subsequently, read the *Guru Gita*. It contains the spiritual instructions imparted by Lord Shiva to Goddess Parvathi. Let at least some of your doubts be resolved through that text. The remainder will naturally follow through direct experience. This Kaliyuga possesses a highly unique characteristic. We have been conditioned to believe that Kali is inherently evil. Satyayuga, Tretayuga, Dwaparayuga, and Kaliyuga—these four epochs collectively constitute a Chaturyuga. All human beings born in the fourth quarter of this Chaturyuga—Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras—must experience both good and evil equally and attain liberation in their progressive journey toward the ultimate truth. This principle is not stated differently for anyone. The Brahmin, whose supremacy was established by the Brahminical religion through Vedic tenets and Tantric practices, holds no legitimate place here. The Kshatriyas, who executed royal governance utilizing their education, wealth, and enlightenment, also have no place. If the era of the Devas was culminated through magical and Tantric methodologies during the Tretayuga and Dwaparayuga, the epoch of Kali must be fulfilled through profound penance (Tapas) and supreme wisdom (Jnana). Penance, in this context, is the formidable ascetic power attained through righteous action; it is not acquired by retreating into a forest. That comprehensive action—action encompassing all dimensions such as thought, word, and deed—will systematically engender both fundamental purity and supreme sanctity. Through this transformative process, spiritual merit (Punya) will invariably manifest as an inherent trait. Undoubtedly, when one accrues spiritual merit, divine fortune will perpetually accompany it. It is proclaimed that this very fortune can empower one to claim the right to ultimate liberation (Mukti). One may designate it as 'Yoga' if so desired. This is precisely the doctrine articulated in the *Bhagavad Gita*. Act by thoroughly assimilating the profound words of the Supreme Soul Sri Krishna: "Buddhyayukto Yoga balena" (Act with the formidable power of Yoga seamlessly united with the intellect). This will subsequently pave the definitive way for liberation. This is the paramount Dharma of Kali. It is fundamentally because the Tantric dominance of the Brahmin and the sovereign administrative rule of the Kshatriya have been irrevocably dismantled that the priestly scholars deceptively propagate the notion that Kaliyuga is entirely worthless. That is not the factual truth. On this auspicious day, I am formally recording these profound words for you, seamlessly incorporating my own spiritual experience.

I am reminding you once again to ensure the absolute culmination of the essential duties that were previously brought to your attention and which you have only partially executed. Everyone must undoubtedly remember how we desperately wandered in search of drinking water two years ago. There were even individuals who deeply pondered whether Kerala would perish entirely due to a devastating drought unprecedented in recent times. During that critical period, prayer assemblies were conducted continuously from Santhigiri across various locations, actively involving both believers and non-believers. You are thoroughly convinced that everything stated back then was the absolute truth. In the geological history of this Earth, which remains a relatively small sphere revolving within the orbital path of the solar system, India, situated prominently along the equator, inherently possesses an almost temperate climatic system. I am articulating this without forgetting the empirical fact that extreme heat and cold are occasionally experienced in certain regions here as well. However, when objectively compared to other nations, we primarily experience a highly temperate climate. This is exceptionally true concerning Kerala. We are all thoroughly cognizant of the historical condition wherein Kerala was virtually a terrestrial paradise when compared to states like Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh. Yet today, systematically reversing that idyllic state, various specific committees and assemblies have been strategically established here to firmly entrench Tantric practices and the orthodox Brahminical religion, functioning in a destructive manner that eradicates intrinsic spiritual merit and leads the very nation toward its ruin. You are well aware that as a direct historical consequence of their past actions, immediately subsequent to the onset of Kaliyuga, our nation was tragically lost into the subjugating hands of numerous foreign invaders. The frenzied oracles of Tantric practices are once again aggressively roaring with rhythmic percussion, dance, and song, deliberately obscuring the grim historical reality that we not only lost India's vast economic wealth but were also stripped of our indigenous modes of worship, traditional attire, and native language, thereby being universally reduced to abject slavery. Alongside this chaotic scenario, several individuals superficially labeling themselves as believers and non-believers are wandering aimlessly in utter intellectual confusion. Those who ostentatiously claim to be non-believers have readily adopted the alien attire and language of foreigners, overflowing with the arrogant delusion that the absolute core of all knowledge resides exclusively within them; they have tragically transformed into sterile intellects, much like the barren arrogance of a mature yet entirely leafless tree. Nothing whatsoever emanates from their literary endeavors except a profoundly putrid stench. The piercing arrows of so-called 'modernity' have been conveniently provided to them as ideological weapons for this destructive purpose. They completely fail to realize that they and this aggressively roaring mob of pseudo-believers are not two distinct entities, but fundamentally one and the same. It is merely akin to the myriad waves of the ocean roaring and crashing individually. Every single wave violently strikes the shore driven by the forceful ego of asserting its own supremacy. The exhausted and systematically impoverished masses, who innocently believe all this spectacle to be the ultimate truth, must consciously avoid falling into these deceptive traps and losing their spiritual bearing; instead, they must meticulously investigate and comprehend the inherent Dharma of this specific era. As long as we physically exist on this earth, if consuming food and drinking water is an absolute biological necessity for us, we must concurrently cultivate profound spiritual merit in a harmonious manner that does not violate or alter the fundamental, immutable laws of nature. In this noble pursuit, all human beings are fundamentally equal. There is absolutely no distinction between the erudite scholar and the unlettered commoner. There is no discriminatory differentiation between a Kshatriya and a Vaishya.

From the Santhigiri Ashram, you have been repeatedly and emphatically reminded of this in the following manner. In this earthly realm, the present epoch is unequivocally the Kaliyuga. The Satyayuga, Tretayuga, and Dwaparayuga each possessed their own distinct and specific Dharmas. During those respective historical periods, those designated principles were duly and systematically executed. If such was indeed the historical precedent, we must firmly and logically believe that Kaliyuga also possesses a specific, inherent Dharma. What was scripturally documented in the specific context of Devas and Devis has already been comprehensively practiced until the historical culmination of the Dwaparayuga. The Supreme Soul Sri Krishna has conclusively proven this fundamental truth, visibly demonstrating it by appropriately acting and facilitating designated actions. Critically examine the eminent Yugapurushas (epochal spiritual figures) who have emerged since that era. In the Western nations, numerous divine mandates have been successfully established through the profound ministries of Jesus, Moses, and the Prophet. Concurrently, within that same historical timeframe in our own land, from Sri Krishna to Buddha, Vardhamana Mahavira, Dayananda Saraswati, the profound preceptors belonging to the illustrious lineage of the *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam*, countless solitary Mahatmas, and within Kerala itself, spiritual luminaries like Sri Narayana Guru, Chattampi Swamikal, and Sri Shankaracharya—all these great souls have unequivocally and repeatedly exhorted us to live harmoniously and fraternally like the children of a single father; deeply contemplate upon the absurdities and contradictions we are currently perpetrating in the sacred presence of their monumental spiritual legacies.

I am reminding you once again. If we are to successfully avoid wandering endlessly in a desperate search for essential drinking water and food, we must sincerely and exclusively engage in monotheistic prayer directed solely to the One Supreme God, rather than blindly and futilely chasing after numerous demigods and subordinate deities. It is precisely to impart this profound realization that these great souls have been prominently highlighted. We are not intellectually bankrupt people who fail to comprehend any of this. Instead of finding false, momentary solace in witnessing aimlessly wandering spectacles—such as the bizarre ritualistic aberrations in Tamil Nadu, the extreme worship practices resembling cannibalistic savagery in Rajasthan, or the demonic, self-destructive savagery of leaping into blazing fire pits in Lanka—we must consciously awaken with rational wisdom and spiritual clarity. By artificially categorizing spiritual paths into Mahayana and Hinayana, we must decisively and permanently escape from the deceptive, binding strings of the regressive Tantric practices that have once again thrust us downward into a lesser spiritual trajectory. Emphasizing once again the undeniable and absolute truth that the 'Path of the Guru' (Gurumargam) is unconditionally essential for this ultimate salvation, I solemnly dedicate these words to you.
Your Swami,
Guruvani
October 1986

Today, the actions we perform concerning the concept of God are typically conceptualized through various forms and attributes. However, some individuals differ, often perceiving this in an illusory manner. Others conceptualize the divine nature as absolute nothingness, without any specific objective, yet omnipresent and pervading everything. Humanity was created by endowing it with form, expression, and action. Consequently, a person's conceptualizations and emotional expressions develop in alignment with their mental maturation. Through such conceptual frameworks, great souls have emerged and departed in accordance with the *Yuga Dharma* (the duty of the epoch). It is customary for us to regard the extraordinary power associated with their concepts as the very concept of God. This subsequently transitions into a form of worship. Initially, we lacked the capacity to worship or even conceive of such a phenomenon. There existed such an era. After all, in the beginning, humanity experienced a primitive state, incapable of cooking food or wearing clothes. Later, through the progressive development of the human intellect, and by imparting expression, form, and love, those actions were cultivated. The spiritual power of such souls has flourished and exists today. This is precisely how every object we currently utilize was conceptualized. Following this conceptualization, humanity learned the appropriate and inappropriate applications of these creations. Thus, through the continuous discernment of the good, we comprehended the nature of life's actions.

Since today is the atomic age, you can understand this in every way. Today, there is a course of action to examine and know what exists on earth, in the sky, and in other celestial bodies. We happened to be born, grow up, and experience this in such an era. If we had lived ten or two hundred years ago, we would not have been able to use or even imagine these motor services and other vehicles that we see today and use daily. Similarly, electricity, as seen today, could not have been conceived in those times. Today, so many things have been invented for human comfort. Whether sitting at home or anywhere else, events happening in every corner of the world are visualized and seen in the same form, expression, and emotion as if they were happening right here. This is the merit of our times. This is *Kali*. Therefore, it is impossible to describe what can be achieved when the *Kali Yuga* progresses further. This demonstrates the magnitude of human invention. At the same time, it was somewhat similar in the ancient times of the Devas, only their methods were different. It is said that they chanted mantras to release weapons and suspended things in the atmosphere through sheer willpower. Such things have occurred since time immemorial. However, we should not assume that this happened to everyone at all times. Back then, things could only happen that way. Consequently, the human mind was directed toward that path, and that path was continuously strengthened. Strengthening through mantras, strengthening through form and expression—all these were brought into action. Through the same imagination, it remains effective in the atmosphere, within us, and in each of the celestial spheres, proportional to the magnitude of that concept. However, as time progressed, we have grown into the knowledge to think, make others think, learn, and teach beyond those ancient methods.

Today, we are situated within the *dharma* and *karma* of the *Kali Yuga*. We have attained things easily today. Those who lived two hundred years ago could not have even dreamed of any of this in reality. We are strengthened in such an action. However, in the *dharma* of *Kali*, there is something we need to attain profoundly. We must realize it through self-actualization. Just like our concepts and actions, a concept and action specific to this *Kali Yuga* must exist in the world. What are they? We must continuously perform virtue-dense actions through conceptual manifestation, eliminating the negative aspects of the past, elevating them to higher planes, and establishing them in the world as a domain of action (*karma kanda*) on our behalf. For this purpose, we have received guidance through divine revelations and spiritual visions. Having been blessed to partake in this monumental task, we must possess the absolute certainty that we can accomplish this—which represents the highest of merits, the greatest of actions, and the pinnacle of wisdom. If we, who are entirely convinced of this truth, treat this matter trivially while being recipients of the era's potential, it would be a profound disrespect toward the Divine. It would also befall us as one of the greatest sins. Therefore, regardless of whether we are sick or healthy, young or old, or whoever we may be, it makes no difference in this regard. This is an action that affords us the opportunity to perceive everything as one. Saying that everything is one does not imply that all human beings are identical. However, in terms of merits and demerits, there will be minor variations according to their individual abilities, tastes, and colors. The eligibility for experience will be more or less the same. Medicine may act quickly for some, while for others, it may not. It will succeed or fail depending on one's inherent karmic tendencies. Similarly, someone may be able to make inventions swiftly, while others can understand things immediately upon hearing them. Someone else might be able to manifest something into action merely by visualizing it from afar. Such variations exist. This is the truth. Therefore, one should not claim, "Only what I have seen is right," or "Only what you have seen is right." What everyone has perceived is indeed correct. It is a state of awareness cultivated by performing actions while rooted in one's respective imagination. However, a shortcoming has occurred among our ancestors. A habit has developed where past eras are pushed back, and only those past times are acknowledged. That is insufficient for us. We must give importance to the era we are living in, highlight past actions, undertake what can be practiced from them, preserve their goodness, discard the evil if it must be discarded, halt what needs to be halted in its proper place, and harmonize the conceptual methodology, action, and wisdom required for this world.
Guru Vani
November 1986

Initially, there was only a very small hut in Santhigiri. A hut just about my height. Only if one stood exactly in the middle would their head not hit the roof. In every stage of growth, we must be able to reflect from the very beginning. What myriad hardships were overcome since those days to reach this point? Within a year, we managed to build a small prayer room in place of that little hut. It was only after seven years and four months that people began arriving, recognizing it as a place of worship. Today, it has reached this state. You must realize how much hardship brimmed with the profound response of goodness within this journey. You must understand that whenever goodness is about to occur, it is preceded by an element of evil. From that time until today, this has been my experience. If the impending goodness is monumental, it will be preceded by a situation where people collectively criticize or speak ill. If it is minor, it will be some other situation that causes mental anguish. If it is even smaller, at least a little child will cause us some pain. Something of that nature must occur. That is the reaction of goodness. However, ordinary people believe that sorrow should never befall them. We even have a system for that—offerings (*nercha*). If they hear that going to a particular place will ward off sorrow, they will rush there. Yet, we do not visit such sacred places merely to prevent sorrow. It is to inquire and understand our joys and sorrows, to discover what solutions exist for them, and to explore the possibilities within our lives to alter the state of our soul. It is to recognize the potential disruptions that may arise from our course of action, to work through them, and to attain the opportunity to become the true masters of our own *karma*.

In the karma of gods and goddesses, they revel in numerous joys and sorrows, immerse themselves in it, and are then forced to take birth again. However, this is not what is said about human beings. But it is the singing of praises and rituals of the gods and goddesses that you have learned. You sing praises to the gods and consider it to be everything. This is similar to some emotional people who love someone deeply and then stand ready to hang themselves. If asked why, even they would not know. Similarly, when these special praises, with their repetitive power, reach our karma, it becomes equivalent to hanging our lives. However, they have stated in one word—in the Satya Yuga, penance is required; in the Treta and Dvapara Yugas, manifesting the deity and offering praise; and in the Kali Yuga, chanting of names. They haven't specified whose name. Therefore, even in the Kali Yuga, we merely chant the root mantras (moola mantras). Scholars have written that salvation (Sayoojyam) can be attained through this. By bestowing all forms of mastery upon the gods and making us worship them, they are kept pleased. The enlightened ones stand above this and speak of the Upanishads. There are Upanishads written by scholars. In them, depicting such descriptions, those who consumed liquor (Sura) from the enlightened kings of that time were preserved as Devas (gods). Thus, those who consumed the liquor and meat offered to the gods became Suras. Those who did not became Asuras. The people who are categorized as Asuras belong to the Shudra class. This Shudra class constitutes about eighty percent. All of them might turn into Asuras. You yourself should ponder the reason for this.

This Shudra class encountered a peril in the beginning. It can be untied if one tries, but as long as it remains untied, it continues to be an affliction. This is expressed in a verse in the Bhagavata.
Karma acts as bonds for a person.
Liberation certainly comes only when the bonds are severed ٹ

So, even if you have wondered what the method to untie the knots is, you have not been able to untie them so far. That is the greatest of the perils that befell the Shudra class. Praises were written in such a way that it seemed violence and mischief were the virtues of the Kshatriyas, thus instilling cruelty in them and making them great. All forms of growth have been denied to the Shudra class. If any mistake occurs in that, it is enough to give alms to the Brahmin. Furthermore, they taught that if a Brahmin curses someone to death, that too is a blessing. Cursing meant beating to death. How many such stories do we have? Initially, when I said this, those who portrayed it as deliberately spoken to malign the Brahmins are with me today. Today, they are somewhat convinced. I did not say this after studying history. I said it after observing and understanding the ancestors of each class and caste. It is upon seeing that I called it an affliction that one does not know how to untie.

There were no Brahmins in India. Those who were here were the Konkanis. They are still docile people. (I do not forget the fact that some are ready to become violent under the RSS). They were meritorious people who treated snakes and cows alike and lived without hurting anyone. You must understand that a lineage with such merit perished in this manner. The Aryans drove away this Brahmin community, which maintained honesty, from here by copying various intellectual systems. Then they created their own language, their own order of worship, and became gods themselves. That is the trick of the Aryan.

Some of those who were driven away returned. They can be seen in many parts of Kerala. But today, they have no hold anywhere. If anything is fabricated anywhere, it is the tantric knowledge of the old Aryans. Realizing that this fate befell them because they accepted Tantra and Vedic rituals, they have not yet been able to retreat from it. Although an acharya named Madhwa came among them, he led them back to the old ways. You should not assume it is dishonesty. It is honesty. Only by asking that very power of light what went wrong with us will there be a correction for it. That was also difficult to get at that time. Because Madhwacharya had some scholarship, he did not move in that direction. Thus, Madhwa is the acharya who wrote Dvaita as Advaita and asserted that one can attain Advaita from this Dvaita. Consequently, that lineage reached a state where there was neither Dvaita nor Advaita. Worship reverted to those old tantras. Thus, that lineage declined.
We too must be careful not to make a similar mistake. I am not speaking of Advaita here. I am speaking about the purity of karma. You should not eliminate karma by conflating it with Advaita.
Guruvani
December 1986

Question: In the Varnasrama Dharma of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras, the author of the Gita himself has pointed out that Kali is the era of the Shudra, the fourth stage. To bring them to the path of karma, that is, to unite and uplift the Shudra (the ignorant), what should be done, Guru?
Answer: A people can only be united under a single ideology! And that too, only an ideology in accordance with the Yuga Dharma.

Question: Given that only an ideology mature enough to sever the roots of beliefs deeply embedded in the framework of old habits and rules can sprout a change in the hearts of the people in accordance with the dharma of Kali, who will be the authority of that supremely noble ideology, Guru?
Answer: Haven't you seen that the Treta and Dvapara Yugas have proven that the Yugacharya will be the authority of the Yuga Dharma? Kali also has such authorities.
Question: How can that great soul be found, Guru?
Answer: When karma is increased and merit is attained, that path will become clear.
Question: For those engaged in industry and commerce for their daily livelihood, by what virtuous deed will they attain it?
Answer: When the Western policy of destroying nations and draining wealth through industry and commerce is abandoned, both will be purified.
Question: How can ordinary individuals achieve this?

Answer: First, each individual must maintain purity and moderation in their own thoughts and actions. Goddess Lakshmi and Goddess Saraswati were the sources of wealth. The lineage of acharyas, who had nothing, acquired wealth through their own karma and meditation. Each individual must take a firm vow that we should be able to become a generation capable of passing it on to the next generation. His education and culture began with the acharya. Even his letters began with the acharya's first letter, and he should be able to live a life of dedication.

Man's karma and dharma constitute his greatness. It should be the acharya who makes the people perform karma and gets it done. Even prompting thoughts about the goal of human birth stems from the acharya's adherence to ideals.

The systems of justice conceived by human intellect are not sufficient to sustain human dharma. People do not even think about the necessity of writhing and twisting, claiming it to be devotion. They do not consider the basis for dismissing something by saying, 'This is Kali.' Today's order, discipline, civilization, and intellect are not those of the olden times. Man can only be guided through methods suited to the times. The culture with its ancient heritage is becoming unknown to today's generation. We are the remnants of having lived as slaves due to a lack of wealth and knowledge, devoid of freedom and culture. Many acharyas came and tried to change this. They failed. The Shudra culture extinguished the ignorant people's inclination to embrace the acharya. When wealth and position came, the Shudra became arrogant. Arrogance destroyed the clan. Even the Brahmins of India fell under the spell of the Westerner's whiteness—possessing a Vedic demeanor but the karma of a Shudra.

The people stood in wonder before the demon-dancers, much like a job-seeker before a palmist. Scholars focused only on making shelves, buying books, reading, and filling them up. No one could save the people from this. Only an enlightened Acharya can save them. One can live in accordance with Dharma only when they are able to internalize the Acharya. Only through that can virtuous deeds be performed.
Guru Vani
